technical_and_design_decisions: Use Spring Security for implementing file-based and LDAP authentication (U1, U2).
Leverage Spring Security's role-based access control for Admin/Viewer roles (U3).
Integrate Spring Security Kerberos for securing HDFS sink (U4).
Use Spring Integration for JMX source module (U8).
Implement HBase sink using Spring Data HBase for random read/write access (U6).
Create a custom File Roll sink module for local file system storage (U7).
Treat U5 as a spike to research and document mass-ingestion design options without implementation.
Assume existing project structure uses Spring Boot with Java 17+ and modular architecture.
assumptions: The project is a Spring Boot application with existing modules for JDBC and other sinks/sources.
Kerberos and LDAP infrastructure (servers, configurations) are pre-configured and accessible.
HBase and Hadoop clusters are available for testing Kerberos and HBase sink integrations.
File-based security configurations will use standard Spring Security properties files.
The spike (U5) will not include implementation, only design documentation and collaboration.
All endpoints (http://localhost:9393/) are already defined and require security encapsulation.
JMX notifications will be consumed via Spring Integration's JMX support.
File Roll sink will write events to a local directory with basic file rotation logic.

activities.activity_description: Implement Spring Security with file-based authentication for all endpoints (U1).
Configure LDAP authentication and integrate with Spring Security (U2).
Define Admin/Viewer roles and enforce access control on endpoints (U3).
Implement Kerberos authentication for secure HDFS data writes (U4).
Research integration options, collaborate on design, and document outcomes (U5).
Develop HBase sink for random, real-time read/write access (U6).
Implement File Roll sink for local file system event storage (U7).
Create JMX source for publishing/subscribing to JMX notifications (U8).
